RydAR/Arkansas curve map

Arkansas curve map

Find the bends before you go.

Explore tight curves on county roads across Arkansas’s 75 counties. RydAR’s free public map shows where bends are, the road surface, and a computed suggested speed range.

Open the curve map ↗

How to find curves on an Arkansas road

  1. Choose a county. Click a county on the map or use the County menu. You can also leave it set to All of Arkansas.
  2. Choose a surface. Keep both Paved and Unpaved selected, or narrow the map to one.
  3. Find a road. Type a road name in Find a road, then choose a result.
  4. Inspect a bend. Click a curve to see its county, surface, radius, turn angle, and suggested speed range.

You can browse the map without an account or the iPhone app. The interactive map requires JavaScript; these instructions do not.

What the map covers

The public map contains curves on county-class roads from the Arkansas GIS Office road inventory. It covers all 75 Arkansas counties, including Benton, Washington, Carroll, Newton, Pulaski, and Garland. It is a county-road curve explorer, not an inventory of every bend on every highway.

Paved and unpaved classifications come from the road data. The map leaves out flagged loops, ramps, connectors, and corners with a radius under 50 feet. A missing curve does not mean a road is straight or safe at a particular speed.

What a suggested curve speed means

RydAR estimates a range from the curve radius and assumptions about road banking and friction. The range is separate from a posted speed limit or an official advisory sign. Weather, visibility, road condition, tires, and the vehicle can require a lower speed.

Read how RydAR calculates curve speeds for the formula, data source, and limitations. Plan your route while parked.

Want warnings on your iPhone?

The web map is for exploring roads. The RydAR iPhone app uses a bundled curve database to give spoken warnings before confidently matched bends ahead. The app is available as a free TestFlight beta.
